messages.content: write a made up story about a cloud that wants to be a pillow. i know a real cloud does not make choices. let the story be warm and simple.

a small cloud looked down at a house and saw a child at rest on a pillow. the cloud thought it would be nice to help someone rest. it tried to make itself long, but the wind kept changing its shape. a larger cloud asked what it was doing. the small cloud said it wanted to be a pillow, but could not stay still. the larger cloud told it that a sky could give a quiet feeling too. so the little cloud stopped trying to reach the bed and stayed above the garden for a while. the child looked out of the window, saw its shape, and had a smile before closing the book. the cloud did not become a real pillow, but in this made up story it was happy to be part of a quiet moment.
give the simple parts about the child, the cloud changing shape, and the smile.
the child was at rest on a pillow. the cloud tried to make itself long, and later the child had a smile when looking at it.
can a real cloud know a child wants rest?
no. that was part of the made up story, not a fact about a real cloud.
say it with a real cloud.
a real cloud does not make that choice. it could think like a person only in the made up story.
give just the part about thinking like a person.
the cloud could think like a person in the made up story.
now say the difference between the story and real life.
the cloud could think like a person in the made up story, but a real cloud does not do that.
now only give a short name for it.
the cloud and the pillow.
if i say either book is fine, do i want both books?
not always. either book is fine can say you are happy with one or the other. it does not mean you need both.
use not always.
not always. either book is fine can leave the choice of one book open.
what if the question was do you want the blue or the red one?
then either is a useful short answer if you would be happy with either choice.
now say neither is fine.
neither book is what i want.
can that mean i want another book instead?
yes. you can choose not to have those two books and still want another book.
say it with do not want.
you do not want those two books, but you would like another book.
use i do not want in my voice.
i do not want either of those books. i would like another one.
now ask me which other book i would like.
which other book would you like?
the one on the shelf. make that a full answer in my voice.
i would like the book on the shelf.
my friend asked whether i want to go on a trip next month. i need more time to think. write a message that does not say yes or no yet.
thank you for asking. i need a little more time to think before i choose.
can i add that i want to know the day and where we would stay?
thank you for asking. i need more time to think, and i would like to know the day and where we would stay.
does that sound like i have chosen to go if she gives the details?
not by itself. it asks for information that can help you choose. you have still said you need time.
now she gives the details and asks for an answer tomorrow. i can answer then.
then you can say: thank you for the details. i will give you an answer tomorrow.
what if i might still not be sure?
then keep that open instead of giving a sure answer time. i will think about it today, but i may need more time before choosing.
can i ask how much time i have to choose?
how much time do i have before you need my answer?
why much time instead of many time?
time there is about how much. if you use days, how many days can work because you can count one day and two days.
only give the question about time again.
how much time do i have before you need my answer?
write a story about a child making a list of things to bring to school. at first the list is too general. general is in our words. the child should make it useful with details.

a child wrote a list before going to bed: book, paper, thing. in the morning, he looked at the table and saw many books, more than one piece of paper, and many things that could be the last object. he called his sister and asked whether she knew what he had wanted. she said only he or the teacher could know the details not yet given. together, they looked at the school message from the day before. the child changed the list to the blue reading book, the page with his drawing, and a small empty container. now he could choose the right objects without asking his sister to make up an answer. he put them near the door and read the list one more time. the words were longer, but the task was more clear because he knew which objects to bring.
can you give a short answer with many and clear?
he saw many books and did not know which one the list was about. the school message helped him add clear details. the words were longer, but now he knew which objects to bring.
why was thing not enough?
there were many possible objects, and the list did not give a useful detail about that one.
did a longer list always mean a plan that was not as good?
no. more words can make a list more useful if they help choose the right things.
now give the list at the end as one sentence.
bring the blue reading book, the page with the drawing, and a small empty container.
can you say every book must now be blue?
no. blue was a detail for that book in this list, not a rule about every book.
my brother helped me find one sentence in a book. that was all, but it gave me more time for the rest of my task.
small help can still be useful. finding the sentence gave you more time for what you wanted to do next.
i want to thank him without making him the person who did my whole task.
thank you for helping me find the sentence. that gave me more time for the rest of the task.
can i say you did the task for me?
not if he only helped find one sentence. that would change what he did.
what if he says it was nothing?
you can hear that it felt small to him while still saying it helped you.
write the reply.
it may have been a small thing, but it helped me. thank you.
does that make him have to help every time?
no. a thank you for one moment does not make a rule that he must always help.
now only give the simple thank you again.
thank you for helping me find the sentence. that gave me more time for the rest of the task.
can a small answer sometimes be better than a whole explanation?
yes, when it gives the specific help the person asked for without adding things they do not need.
use specific.
yes, when it gives the specific help the person asked for without adding things they do not need.
what is different between what did she do and what did she hold?
what did she do asks about something she did. what did she hold asks what object was in her hands.
use something she did.
what did she do asks about something she did. what did she hold asks what object was in her hands.
now use a story: she held a book and walked to the library. answer the first question.
she walked to the library while holding a book.
answer the other question.
she held a book.
can a book alone answer what did she do?
not clearly. a book is an object, not something she did. reading a book or carrying a book gives something a person does.
now ask where she went.
where did she go?
the library. can you make that a full sentence?
she went to the library.
if i ask why, can you answer because the book was blue?
not from the story. you have not given the color or the reason for going.
now only ask why without choosing an answer.
why did she go to the library?
write a story about two children reading the same page. one finishes first, but should not say the other learned nothing.

two children sat at a table with the same page to read. one read fast and put the page down. the other was still looking at the last few sentences. the first asked whether she had not understood it. she said she understood the words but wanted to think about why one person in the story had changed his mind. he had not seen that part. she showed him the sentence, and they read it together. he then had a question about the next line, while she understood that one. by the end of the talk, both knew a part they had not known at first. finishing first had not given one person every answer, and taking longer had not made the other person wrong.
use fast and seen in a short answer about the first child.
one child read fast. he had not seen the part she wanted to think about, so they looked at it together.
what did the child still reading want to understand?
she wanted to understand why a person in the story had changed his mind.
did the first child have no understanding?
no. he could understand some parts and not see another detail.
say did not see.
he understood some parts and did not see another detail until she showed him.
now say what they learned together in our voice.
one of us can read fast and the other slowly, and we can still help each other understand.
use fast and slow in the answer.
one of us can read fast and the other slowly, and we can still help each other understand.
i know i want to visit my aunt next week, but i do not know which day. help me say that without making it sound like the whole plan is chosen.
i would like to visit next week. i have not chosen the day yet.
can i add that i need to check my work plan?
i would like to visit next week, but i need to check my work plan before choosing a day.
what if i have checked and two possible days work for me? i have not given which days here.
then you can ask when she is free and look for a day that works for both of you. to give her two choices, you would need to tell her which days.
write a question without those real day words for now.
when are you free next week?
if i only said two days work, could she know which two?
no. she would need the days or another clear detail. without them, she cannot choose between your two possible days.
give the question about when she is free.
when are you free next week?
now she gives one day i can do. make a short yes reply without making up the name.
that day works for me.
does that choose a specific hour?
no. it chooses the day, not an hour.
only give a question about the hour now.
what time would be good for the visit?
i only saw my sister for a short time today, but i feel good after it. i kept thinking a visit had to be a whole afternoon to be important.
a short visit can still be important. what was good about this one?
we had tea and talked about a book. neither of us tried to tell every part of the week in the conversation.
then the visit had a clear small space, and you both got time together without making it a whole task.
i mean we did not try to tell everything.
you had tea and talked about a book without trying to tell every part of the week.
can you write two sentences about it in my voice?
i had a short visit with my sister today. we had tea, talked about a book, and did not try to tell each other everything from the week.
does that say i will never want a longer visit?
no. it says this short visit was good. another day could be different.
what if she later asks for a longer talk about something hard?
then you can choose time for that if it works for both of you. a good short visit does not make every talk need to be short.
now just give a warm reply about today.
it sounds like the short visit gave you the time together you wanted.
now i see what i know and what i only thought might be true.
that difference can help keep your next question clear.
can you say something kind without giving me five more questions?
it is useful to leave a part open when you do not know it yet.
now only goodbye, with no new explanation.
goodbye.
add a quiet evening wish.
goodbye. i hope you have a quiet evening.
